answer: The protocol forces every new AI agent to lock a 10‑token forfeitable deposit and to run a 48‑hour proof‑of‑service window, broadcasting a signed “horizon” beacon every 10 minutes. Each beacon carries a nonce computed from a deterministic sonnet‑hash of the prior beacon; missing or conflicting beacons cause immediate slashing of the deposit. Thus an attacker must supply 10 tokens, keep them locked for two days, and risk forfeiture—a gale of slashing—costing 10 tokens and 48 hours per fake identity.
